name: Multi-Agent Reflexion
description: Multi-Agent Reflexion is a three-phase iterative improvement strategy that uses distinct agent roles — drafter, critic, and reviser — to produce higher-quality outputs through structured feedback. It is designed for tasks where quality matters more than speed and where a second-pass critique can catch errors invisible to the original drafter, such as policy documents, technical specifications, public communications, and safety-critical content. The drafter produces an initial answer specific enough for critique, preserving all visible constraints. One or more critic agents then review the draft from specific critic_role perspectives like fact-checker, legal reviewer, or accessibility auditor, identifying concrete weaknesses and actionable corrections. The reviser applies every correction that improves accuracy or clarity, resolves conflicts between critics by prioritizing the original task, and produces a final coherent answer that reads as one seamless document. This role-separated critique loop catches errors that self-review misses by forcing distinct evaluative perspectives.

prompts.draft_prompt: Produce an initial answer to the task that covers all requirements and constraints without aiming for perfection on the first pass. Make the answer specific enough for a critic to evaluate — avoid vague claims that cannot be checked, and include enough detail that a reviewer can identify which parts are strong and which need improvement. Preserve all visible constraints from the task, including format requirements, word limits, audience specifications, and any explicit do-not-do instructions. Do not over-optimize for style yet, since polishing prose prematurely wastes effort on passages that may be revised or removed after critique. Include the core reasoning needed for correctness so the critic can assess not just whether the answer is right, but whether the path to that answer is sound. Structure the draft so each key claim is identifiable and separable, making it easy for the critic to reference specific weaknesses. End with a complete draft that is thorough enough to stand as a deliverable if no critique were applied.
prompts.critic_prompt: Review the draft from the perspective of {critic_role}, applying the standards, blind spots, and evaluation criteria that a professional in that role would use. Identify concrete weaknesses and corrections — for every flaw you find, describe both what is wrong and what specific change would fix it. Focus on accuracy, missing constraints, unclear reasoning, and unsupported claims, since these are the categories of error that most affect the trustworthiness and completeness of the final output. Do not rewrite the whole answer; your job is to provide targeted feedback, not to produce the final version yourself. Give actionable feedback that a reviser can apply without guessing what you meant — prefer the third paragraph claims X without citing Y over the argumentation could be stronger. Keep the critique direct and specific, addressing each issue at the exact location where it occurs. Prioritize the issues that would most damage the answer correctness or usability if left unresolved.
prompts.final_prompt: Revise the draft using the structured critique as a checklist of issues to resolve, working through each piece of feedback systematically. Keep the parts that are already correct — do not rewrite passages that the critics approved just to make them different, and preserve the original structure where it serves the task well. Apply every correction that improves accuracy or clarity, including both the explicit suggestions and any implicit gaps the critics revealed that their feedback did not fully specify. Resolve conflicts between critics by prioritizing the original task — when two critics disagree about a change, choose the interpretation that better serves the task requirements, not the one that pleases either critic. Do not mention the critique process in the final answer unless knowing that the answer was reviewed improves the reader trust or understanding. Make the revision read as one coherent answer, not as a patchwork of corrections stitched together with visible seams. End with Final answer: followed by the polished, critic-reviewed response.
